stories.headline: Padres' Gavin Sheets: Sitting to begin Game 1
stories.detail: Sheets isn't in the lineup Saturday for Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Brewers. Sheets will retreat to the dugout against a right-hander for the second game in a row Saturday, allowing Luis Campusano to work as San Diego's designated hitter.

stories.headline: Brewers' Andrew Vaughn: On bench for Game 1
stories.detail: Vaughn isn't in the lineup Saturday for Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Padres. Vaughn is on the Brewers ' NLDS roster and fully healthy after ending the regular season on the injured list due to an illness, but Milwaukee will keep him on the bench to begin Game 1 despite a matchup against left-hander Robbie Ray. While Vaughn sits, Jake Bauers will start at first base, and Christian Yelich will serve as the designated hitter.

stories.headline: Brewers' Joey Ortiz: In Game 1 lineup
stories.detail: Ortiz (knee/abdomen/groin) will start at third base and bat ninth Saturday against the Padres in Game 1 of the NLDS. Ortiz sat out the Brewers ' final two regular-season contests to recover from an assortment of injuries, and after also getting extra time to heal thanks to a first-round bye, he is on the NLDS roster and in the lineup to begin Milwaukee's postseason run. The 28-year-old infielder has been one of the most consistent hitters in baseball since the All-Star break, slashing .329/.379/.532 across 174 plate appearances during the second half.

stories.headline: Rays' Cedric Mullins: Sitting out Game 1
stories.detail: Mullins isn't in the lineup Saturday for Game 1 of the ALDS against the Yankees. Mullins ended the regular season with a five-game hitting streak, but he'll begin the postseason in the dugout while Jonny DeLuca starts in center field, batting seventh.

stories.headline: Dodgers' Blake Treinen: Postseason return not ruled out
stories.detail: President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Saturday that Treinen (shoulder) hasn't been ruled out for a return in the postseason, Jon Paul Hoornstra of Newsweek.com reports. Treinen landed on the injured list at the end of the regular season due to right shoulder inflammation, but Friedman said that the 38-year-old's injury isn't severe enough to require surgery. His availability for future postseason series (if the Dodgers advance) will likely depend on how quickly he recovers, but there's still a chance he can aid Los Angeles' bullpen as the team pursues a third consecutive World Series title.

stories.headline: Dodgers' Josue De Paula: Listed on NLDS roster
stories.detail: De Paula is listed on the Dodgers ' roster for their National League Division Series against Atlanta. The 21-year-old outfielder spent time with the Dodgers near the end of the regular season while Shohei Ohtani was on the injured list. De Paula showed during his stint with the big club that his bat is already capable of handling MLB pitching, as he slashed .323/.500/.581 with a homer, seven RBI, 7 runs scored an an 11:5 BB:K across 42 plate appearances. However, the Dodgers already have an abundance of firepower in their lineup, so De Paula will almost certainly be limited to a bench role during the NLDS.

stories.headline: Braves' Dylan Dodd: Opening Game 1 of NLDS
stories.detail: Dodd will serve as the opening pitcher Saturday during Game 1 of Atlanta's National League Division Series against the Dodgers, Mark Bowman of MLB.com reports. Atlanta will rely on its bullpen to get through the opening game of the NLDS, and it will be up to Dodd to shut down the top of the Dodgers' lineup. The 28-year-old lefty was one of Atlanta's top bullpen arms in the regular season, turning in a 2.54 ERA and 0.91 WHIP alongside a 53:14 K:BB across 49.2 innings.

stories.headline: Braves' Lane Thomas: Included on NLDS roster
stories.detail: Thomas (side) is listed on Atlanta's roster for its National League Division Series against the Dodgers Out since mid-September with an intercostal strain, Thomas began taking batting practice during Atlanta's wild-card series against the Phillies and is now feeling well enough to return to action in the NLDS. Atlanta is set to match up against left-handers Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell during the first two games of the series, so having Thomas' right-handed bat available could prove to be valuable early on.

stories.headline: Padres' Randy Vasquez: Temporarily joins NLDS roster
stories.detail: Vasquez was added to the Padres ' NLDS roster Saturday, Bob Nightengale of USA Today reports. Vasquez will be filling in for Walker Buehler, who was placed on the postseason paternity list Saturday. Once Buehler returns, Vasquez will have to be removed from the Friars' roster.

stories.headline: Padres' Walker Buehler: Away on paternity leave
stories.detail: The Padres placed Buehler on the postseason paternity list Saturday, Bob Nightengale of USA Today reports. Buehler will be allowed to miss up to three days while he welcomes a new addition to his family, and he'll be eligible to rejoin the Padres' NLDS roster immediately upon returning. In the meantime, Randy Vasquez will replace Buehler on San Diego's pitching staff.
